subject: Food Science
title: Artificial Food Colors
description: A quick, practical guide to Artificial Food Colors.

hook.text: Red 40, Yellow 5, Blue 1—just seven synthetic dyes color most processed food in the US. Europe uses fewer.

buildup.text: Synthetic colors are made from petroleum derivatives. They're brighter, cheaper, and more stable than natural ones.

discovery.text: In 1900, over 80 synthetic dyes were used in food. By 1960, only 7 survived safety testing.

twist.text: The EU requires warning labels on foods with certain dyes: 'may have adverse effect on activity in children.'

climax.text: Many companies reformulated with natural colors for EU markets—but still use synthetic dyes in US products.

punchline.text: Same company, same product, different continents, different dyes. Standards diverge.

quiz.question: How does the EU handle synthetic food dyes differently than the US?
options: EU requires warning labels about potential effects on children's activity
